title: Petrol and Diesel Prices Remain Steady in Major Indian Cities Amid Global Market Volatility
text:
• Petrol and diesel prices in major Indian cities remained unchanged on Thursday.
• Global fuel markets experienced volatility due to the escalating Middle East conflict and concerns over oil supply routes.
• Hyderabad had the highest petrol price among the six major metros at ₹107.46 per litre.
• New Delhi had the lowest petrol price among the six major metros at ₹94.77 per litre.
• Five out of the six major metros reported petrol prices above ₹100 per litre.
• Hyderabad had the highest diesel price among the six major metros at ₹95.70 per litre.
• Delhi had the lowest diesel price among the six major metros at ₹87.67 per litre.
• Andhra Pradesh reported the highest state-wise petrol price at ₹109.93 per litre.
• Andaman and Nicobar Islands had the lowest state-wise petrol price at ₹82.46 per litre.
• Kerala reported the highest state-wise diesel price at ₹96.38 per litre.
• Andaman and Nicobar Islands reported the lowest state-wise diesel price at ₹78.05 per litre.
• Diesel prices in Europe jumped 27% since Friday.
• Benchmark Brent crude surged past $85 a barrel earlier this week.
• The Indian government stated there is sufficient energy reserves and no immediate shortage of petrol, diesel, or cooking gas is expected.
summary: Petrol and diesel prices across major Indian cities remained steady on Thursday, even as global fuel markets saw sharp volatility amid the escalating Middle East conflict and concerns over oil supply routes.Fuel prices remained unchanged from yesterday.ALSO READ | No immediate energy shortage, enough reserves: India amid Middle East tensionsPetrol prices in major cities todayAmong the six key metros, Hyderabad recorded the highest petrol price at ₹107.46 per litre, while New Delhi remained the cheapest at ₹94.77 per litre, HT data showed.Petrol was priced at ₹102.99 in Bengaluru, ₹100.80 in Chennai, ₹105.41 in Kolkata and ₹103.54 in Mumbai per litre.
